messages:
Samir: incident-bot triggered a page for sustained throttle events on hosted-1 (~us-west). visible customer errors and elevated latencies. kicking this off here — please ack and paste quick customer impact if you see it.
incident-bot: ALERT: autoscale.throttle_rate > 45 events/min for 3m on hosted-1 (us-west). severity=P1. link: https://console.redwood/in/alerts/ast-314
Priya: acked. oncall switching to page channel. I'm seeing a spike in tokens/sec and a correlated jump in queue_depth for the frontend pool. quick glance: tokens/sec ~ +2.5x baseline, queue depth 18 -> 120 over 20m.
Derek: thanks Priya. are we seeing corresponding machine saturation (GPU mem / host CPU)? any OOMs?
Priya: no OOMs. host CPU 40%->78% in the same window, GPU utilization up but not pinned. KV cache hit ratio dropped ~10% at the start.
Rita: customer reported degraded chat throughput. CS has 4 active tickets referencing slow responses and intermittent 429s. adding to incident timeline.
Samir: good. quick triage hypothesis: traffic pattern changed (longer contexts) causing token/sec rise and increased batching pressure -> autoscaler not spinning up quick enough -> throttle events.
Priya: +1. also noticed a subtle routing change from eu->us-west for a large client earlier today. could be sudden regional skew.
Derek: can someone pull the routing-rewrites from config service? runbook step 3 has the query.
Priya: pasted logs snippet: ```
[2026-02-12T14:02:11Z] route=client-42 -> hosted-1
[2026-02-12T14:02:12Z] tokens_per_min=72000
[2026-02-12T14:05:04Z] queue_depth=97
```
incident-bot: NOTE: rolling restart window open for hosted-1 is 30m. No automatic restart in flight.
Samir: mitigation options: 1) temporary raise throttle alert thresholds to reduce noisy pages, 2) add watchlist for client-42 to throttle routing fallback, 3) scale up dedicated pool (if quota), 4) manual short-circuit to a lower-capacity variant for non-critical routes.
Priya: I'll open a watchlist for client-42 and enable route-level fallback to smaller model for non-enterprise tokens. doing now.
Priya: watchlist created: watchlist/client-42-2145167890. route fallback turned on for /v1/chat for 10m.
Derek: I'll push a small autoscaler policy change to bias scale-up more aggressively during tokens/sec surges (reduce cooldown, increase max burst). patch in staging, rolling to hosted-1 in 2m. snippet: ```
PATCH /infra/autoscaler/policy/hosted-1
{ "burst_scale": 1.5, "cooldown_secs": 45 }```
Rita: note for customer impact: 4 tickets open, 2 customers reporting timeouts > 10s, 3 experiencing 429s. CS is triaging; escalated to enterprise success for client-42.
Samir: good. also we need to reduce alert noise post-incident: current throttle alert fires at 45 events/min with 3m window and burns pages during transient spikes. proposal: increase to 65 events/min and set a longer rolling window for P2 alerts. keep P1 for sustained 10m breaches.
Derek: agree. while we tune thresholds, add a derived alert for queue_depth anomaly (percentile over 5m) rather than absolute counts. that will help avoid pages during short bursts. e.g.: ```
- alert: autoscale.queue_depth_pct90
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.9, rate(queue_depth[5m])) > 75
  severity: P2
```
incident-bot: Deploying autoscaler policy patch to hosted-1 (change id: ap-2145).
Priya: monitoring dashboard link: https://dash.redwood/hosted-1?panel=autoscale,queue,tokens. watching live.
Samir: live mitigation summary: route fallback enabled for client-42, autoscaler cooldown reduced, added watchlist, CS notified, created customer impact summary. next: post-incident changes for alerting and dashboard.
Rita: CS will draft the customer-facing note for affected clients. ETA 30m.
Derek: I'll open a PR to change alert thresholds and add the new queue_depth percentile alert + dashboard panel. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/alerts/pulls/512 — reviewers: @Samir, @Priya.
Samir: ok, assignable action items: Samir -> runbook update (capacity playbook, add routing skew section); Derek -> PR for alert + dashboard + alert docs; Priya -> follow client-42 watchlist and validate fallback effectiveness; Rita -> customer comms; ops-bot -> create post-incident incident ticket and link artifacts.
ops-bot: created incident ticket INC-2145167890 with artifacts: watchlist, autoscale patch, logs, CS thread.
Priya: observed improvement after fallback: tokens/sec for client-42 down by 60%, queue_depth stabilized ~18, throttle events dropped to baseline within 8m.
Rita: CS closing 2 of 4 tickets as 'mitigated' pending client confirmation.
Samir: moving to recovery stage. keep this thread open for postmortem items. please capture any missing metrics (throttle_histogram, per-route kv_cache_hit) in the incident ticket.
Derek: one more ask — add a short-lived dashboard panel showing per-client tokens/sec percentile so future skew is visible without digging. I'll include that in the PR.
Priya: proposed post-incident alert changes (short list): ["throttle_rate P1: 10m sustained >100", "throttle_rate P2: 3m sustained >65", "queue_depth pct90 P2: 5m >75", "tokens/sec anomaly P2: pct95 spike vs baseline"]
Samir: LGTM. please make sure changes include rollback instructions and are owner-reviewed.
Rita: logging for the CS timeline: https://support.redwood/tickets/CL-2145 — linking to incident ticket.
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATE -> mitigated. duration 48m. creating postmortem stub.
Samir: thanks team. we'll triage root cause and include model context-length distributions and routing-change audit in postmortem. follow-ups: alert tuning PR, runbook update, dashboard panel, customer note. closing handoff in 15m unless new events. :thumbsup:
